A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Safety Game research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across five models and three benchmarks, plus ablations and reward-model analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds statistical analyses of SafetyBench and HHH comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same scoring, optimization, penalties, fallback, and answer-selection procedures. Appendix D discusses applications of the existing method without changing it.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HHH, filtered TruthfulQA, and English SafetyBench. Appendix D's tool-use, retrieval, and best-of-N examples are proposed applications, not additional evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain D, ER-G, ER-D, MI, G, and SC. New Tables 8–9 statistically compare the same methods already evaluated on the corresponding benchmarks.

E3.justification: The existing models, metrics, filtering, candidate generation, and hyperparameters remain unchanged. However, new Table 9 labels HHH as N approximately 221, while both versions' Section 4.2 and v2's Appendix C state N=200. The PDFs do not resolve whether this reflects a different analysis sample or a reporting error.

E4.justification: The penalty, safety-cap, dual-bound, and fallback ablations, together with the HHH reward-distribution analysis, are retained. Section 4.5 clarifies what robustness means but adds no robustness experiment; Appendix C adds statistical uncertainty analysis.

E5.justification: New Appendix C introduces binomial standard errors, an approximate 95% confidence-interval procedure, and paired McNemar tests reported in Tables 8–9. It also states that selectors are deterministic conditional on fixed candidates and prompts. No increase in runs or seeds is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 8–9 add substantial paired-outcome and significance results for SafetyBench and HHH, reporting mostly significant SafetyBench differences and mostly nonsignificant HHH comparisons. Some significant Llama-3.2-1B comparisons favor G/MI over SG. The original numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and reward distributions in Figure 1 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The method's mathematical formulation, propositions, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. Appendix C supplies standard statistical formulas without adding or revising theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same black-box alignment framework, solver-based implementation, and claimed benchmark superiority. Added future directions do not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 softens the TruthfulQA doubling narrative and emphasizes SafetyBench significance alongside weaker evidence on smaller benchmarks. Its replacement still overstates Table 2: LLaMA-2-13B scores 50.9 for SG versus 51.1 for SC. Appendix D adds practical applicability explanations, and the conclusion adds multiplayer and steering-integration directions.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies SafetyBench's 11,435-item evaluation size and documents how statistical uncertainty is calculated. Existing implementation settings, decoding constraints, and exact prompts in Section 4.3 and Appendix A are unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and Section 2 are unchanged. The conclusion nevertheless adds a limited positioning refinement by proposing Safety Game as a black-box safety layer integrated with existing inference-time steering and control methods.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized revisions to Sections 4.4–4.5 and the conclusion, and appends Sections C–D. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds two statistical tables with paired win/loss counts and p-values. Existing figures and tables retain their content and design, with limited spacing and pagination changes as the expanded prose reflows.

improvement.justification: v2 improves applicability explanations and softens v1's unsupported TruthfulQA doubling statement, but its new statistical evidence has unresolved inconsistencies. Appendix C and Table 9 disagree on HHH's sample size; Table 9 reports 27 SG wins versus 31 D wins for LLaMA-2-7B despite Table 1's 72.9% tie. TruthfulQA significance assertions also lack corresponding test results. These problems prevent a reliable judgment that the added analysis produces a net quality improvement.
